\caption{The three levels of explanation per study. Faithful: the largest function-preservation error (explained model state against the phenotype, training rows) over the study's explanations. Decomposed: leaves per explanation and granularity, the share of hidden units whose part is at most 6 units wide (depth is not penalised); coarse counts explanations where one part wider than that holds half the hidden units. Understood: verified is the share of leaves the author graded understood in his leaf-by-leaf verification (the measured level; over the explanations with leaf verdicts, count in brackets when fewer than $n$; -- when none has one yet). The remaining columns are automated screens. Probe: the share of leaves whose best library concept grades meaningful (probe score $\geq 0.8$), partial ($\geq 0.5$) or closed-form only, under the probe's simplicity and support conditions (a concept counts only when it is simpler than the leaf, and a binary concept's AUC only against a gate of comparable support); for Connect-4 the domain column counts only domain concepts (threats, open lines, centre, rows, parity), not raw cells. Verifier: the share of leaves the blind verifier graded meaningful, over the explanations with a verdict (count in brackets when fewer than $n$); disagree: leaves graded by both on which the probe and the verifier differ, over those compared. Cells are median [min--max] over the explanations. The ladder rows are plain backprop MLPs of the explanation complexity ladder; the capacity row is the evolved Connect-4 network.}
\label{tab:ch7-levels}
